clue.text: Clear observation: rigged prices preceding bill received in regret

indicators.note: the bill-and-anagram string is taken inside the word for regret

parts.note: pity is regret or sorrow, as in 'what a pity'

indicators.note: says the shuffled letters go before the bill in the inserted string
something rigged has been tampered with, so the letters of prices are rearranged

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone notices that prices have been fixed and that a bill has been taken in, to their regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' gives ERSPIC; 'received in' splits the word for regret after its first letter to take the string inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspicacity is acute insight, the quality of seeing clearly and shrewdly into things.

clue.text: Religious devotee forbidding going under large building? Not entirely

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first
the building word is not given whole: its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building, such as a stately home
a forbidding look is a grim one

explanation.surface: A sombre figure passes beneath some vast structure, with a hint that it is only partly there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims PILE to PIL; 'going under' places GRIM beneath it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim journeys to a shrine out of religious devotion.

clue.text: Hurriedly make approach to wicket

definitions.meaning: to ... a garment or a shelter is to make it quickly
in cricket, the bowler's run to the crease before delivering the ball

explanation.surface: A bowler hurries in towards the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is the set of stumps the bowler aims at, and the run-up is the bowler's approach before releasing the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from one phrasal verb: dressmakers quickly stitch things together, and bowlers sprint in before delivery.

clue.text: Back appearance of carnival city in advert

indicators.note: the city name is placed inside the advert word

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement
Rio de Janeiro is famed for its annual carnival

explanation.surface: A poster on the back page shows the Rio carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior as a noun is the rear or buttocks; as an adjective it means at the back.

clue.text: Sweet honey source curtailed, leading to tantrum

indicators.note: the shortened piece comes first, followed by the next
cut short, so the last letter of the honey word goes

parts.note: a honeycomb, or comb, is where bees store honey
a fit of temper is a tantrum

explanation.surface: A child denied the honeycomb throws a tantrum over sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfit is an old-fashioned confection, a sugar-coated seed or nut.

clue.text: Disapproving noise about hospital describing get-out clause?

indicators.note: the jeer word goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: a catcall is a shrill whistle or jeer of disapproval
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a hospital's attempt to wriggle out of an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is a link word; the question mark admits a catch-all clause is only loosely a get-out.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch-all clause covers every case not otherwise listed, often giving a party an escape route.

clue.text: Gang to work around start of roadworks

indicators.note: the word to goes around the opening letter that follows
only the first letter of roadworks is used

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A gang of labourers goes to work around the start of some roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a group or band of people, much as a gang is.

clue.text: Not truthful about bird staying near the ground

indicators.note: the untruthful word goes round the bird

parts.note: someone lying is not telling the truth
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A deceitful report about a bird that keeps close to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-lying land or mist is situated at a low level, close to the ground.

clue.text: Room in church most suitable to accommodate religious figure

indicators.note: the suitable word takes the saint inside it

parts.note: 'the very thing' means the most suitable thing
ST, short for saint, is a religious figure

explanation.surface: A church room is ideal for housing a statue of a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the room in a church where vestments are kept and clergy robe.

clue.text: Pair coming in also comes down

wordplay.reading: L, S, the inner pair of ALSO, spelt out with a conjunction

parts.note: the two letters in the middle of the word also, written out as a phrase with a joining word between them

explanation.surface: Two travellers are arriving as well, as their plane touches down.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle pair of 'also' is L and S; spelt out in words, that letter pair gives the answer. Most solvers take 'also' as AND and get stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft that lands comes down onto the ground at the end of a flight.

clue.text: Encountered Monroe dancing — measure of pulse

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: the letters of Monroe move about as if dancing

explanation.surface: A meeting with Marilyn Monroe on the dance floor sets the heart racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome ticks out a steady beat, measuring the pulse or tempo of music.

clue.text: Wrong interrupting supporter turning to reload

indicators.note: the combined string is then read backwards
the wrong breaks into the supporter word

parts.note: a helper is a supporter
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A backer turns against someone, wrongly interrupting them as they reload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' puts SIN into HELPER, giving HSINELPER; 'turning' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill up again, as one reloads a gun or restocks a store.

clue.text: Conspirator's heart displayed in conspiracy trial

indicators.note: the central letter is shown inside the conspiracy word

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A plotter's true feelings are revealed during a conspiracy trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' looks like part of the court case, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot scheme or pilot episode is a trial run before the real thing.

clue.text: Fabric, cut in back, put on view

indicators.note: the shortened word is read backwards
the at-home word loses its last letter

parts.note: being in means being at home
to air something is to display it publicly

explanation.surface: A garment's fabric, trimmed at the back, is put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives HOME (as in 'staying in'); 'cut' makes HOM and 'back' turns it to MOH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is yarn or cloth made from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Influence one to limit disadvantage

parts.note: to have a hand in something is to have influence on it
I is the Roman numeral one
to cap is to limit

explanation.surface: Someone uses influence to restrict a rival, putting them at a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is an impediment, as in racing where weight is added to hold back stronger horses.

clue.text: Keenness from Republican entering in urban style?

indicators.note: the party letter goes into the style phrase

parts.note: a la city, after the French à la, means in the manner of the city

explanation.surface: A Republican shows eagerness by adopting a city-slicker manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is cheerful readiness or eagerness to act, a form of keenness.

clue.text: Government statisticians should be involved in official count, it's agreed

indicators.note: the statisticians' initials are put inside the count word

parts.note: a census is an official count of a population
ONS is the UK's Office for National Statistics, the government statistics body

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that state statisticians must take part in the national census.
explanation.walkthrough: The ONS (Office for National Statistics) is the British government agency that runs the census.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general agreement, the position everyone has accepted.

clue.text: Minister: man almost wholly without affectation?

indicators.note: the man word is given all but its last letter

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man
plain means simple and unpretentious

explanation.surface: A clergyman is described as nearly entirely free of pretension.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a minister of religion attached to an institution such as a regiment or college.

clue.text: Ruling group on for blocking demo by end of day

indicators.note: the word on obstructs, sitting in the middle of the demo word

parts.note: a demo, short for demonstration, can be a protest march

indicators.note: only the last letter of day is used

explanation.surface: A ruling elite is all for stopping a protest by the close of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a royal family and its court, the group that rules in a kingdom.

clue.text: Second course displaying a certain style

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: The second course of a meal is served with some flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means fashionable, following the current mode or style.

clue.text: WWII device: a piece of ordnance used around about capital of Germany

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about the initial of Germany
turned around, so the weapon word is read backwards

parts.note: a mine is an explosive weapon

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of Germany

explanation.surface: A wartime explosive is planted around the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is placed at the end despite leading the clue; 'used around' turns MINE into ENIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enigma was the German cipher machine of the Second World War, broken at Bletchley Park.

clue.text: A term full of initiation

parts.note: a word built entirely from beginnings, that is, from the initial letters of other words

explanation.surface: A school term packed with rites of passage for newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiation' suggests induction ceremonies but here means initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as NATO or radar are formed wholly from the first letters of a phrase.

clue.text: Drawing party up for blocking social security payment

indicators.note: the turned party word blocks the middle of the payment word

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the party word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A sketch shows a party held up in favour of blocking welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. 'On the dole' is British for receiving unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodle is an idle sketch or scribble, a casual drawing.

clue.text: Sick coming to doctor's practice

indicators.note: the sick word is attached after the doctor

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
ill means sick

explanation.surface: An ill patient arrives at the GP's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor's practice' reads as a surgery, but 'practice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a repeated exercise, practice to make a routine automatic.

clue.text: Shelter supported by church and old medical practitioner

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece rests on top of the second

parts.note: a lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A shelter, a church and an old-time doctor make a village scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech was an archaic word for a physician, from the bloodsucking worms they applied.

clue.text: Heading for Portsmouth, rambler will seize last food

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of Portsmouth
the wanderer word takes hold of the word for last

parts.note: a rover is someone who rambles about
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: A hiker bound for Portsmouth grabs a final bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Portsmouth is a naval port on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is an old word for food or provisions, especially fodder for animals.

clue.text: Excessive personal documents turned up just the same

indicators.note: in a down clue the combined pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: Too many identity papers kept showing up, all identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same as before, used to avoid repeating something.

clue.text: This person's familiar with wings and flies

definitions.text: This person's familiar with wings and flies

parts.words: This person's familiar with wings and flies
parts.note: suggests a naturalist or bird-watcher, but wings and flies are the side areas and overhead lofts of a theatre stage

explanation.surface: Someone who knows all about birds and insects.
explanation.walkthrough: Wings and flies suggest insects; in a theatre the wings flank the stage and the flies are the space above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre crew member moves scenery about the backstage areas, so knows them intimately.

clue.text: Occupation of note with exterior function

indicators.note: the function word forms the outside, around the note

parts.note: sin is the sine, a trigonometric function
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A job description: a musical note forms the outside of some task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' suggests a job; here it is a protest that occupies a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest in which demonstrators occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Disturbance in elements of various modern truths

indicators.note: the letters are put into various different orders

explanation.surface: Modern assorted truths cause unrest among the basic building blocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements' suggests chemistry, but here means the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm with lightning and rolls of noise is a violent upset in the weather, the elements.
